title: Fang Bo wins first title for 13 years and Honoka Hashimoto takes WTT Contender Istanbul crown
seo_title: WTT Contender Istanbul: Fang Bo and Hashimoto win titles
description: Fang Bo beat Kang Dongsoo 4-1 for his first singles title since 2013, seven months into his Kazakhstan comeback, and Honoka Hashimoto beat Joo Cheonhui.
standfirst: The 34-year-old wild card beat a South Korean chopper in five games, while Japan's top seed recovered from losing the doubles final to beat Joo Cheonhui 4-1.

body: Fang Bo won his first international singles title for 13 years at WTT Contender Istanbul on Sunday, beating South Korea's Kang Dongsoo 11-9, 8-11, 11-8, 11-6, 11-9, and Japan's Honoka Hashimoto took the women's title by beating Joo Cheonhui 4-1.

Fang, 34, is ranked 160th in the world and came into the tournament as a wild card. He retired in 2021 and announced in April that he was coming back to play for Kazakhstan. Seven months later he has a WTT title, his first singles trophy since the 2013 Austrian Open in Wels.
Kang, 32 and ranked 120th, is a defender, and Fang kept attacking his chop with the forehand, taking the first game 11-9 and, after Kang levelled, the third 11-8 and the fourth 11-6.

Kang, who had beaten the third seed, Elias Ranefur, and then Ryoichi Yoshiyama in a deciding game, kept the fifth close, but Fang closed it out 11-9 after 47 minutes. Both players used their timeouts.

The run was built on comebacks and clean sweeps. Fang beat China's Chen Junsong without dropping a game in the last 16, the Czech seventh seed Lubomir Jancarik 3-0 in the quarter-finals and then, on Saturday, [came from two games down against Ricardo Walther](/news/wtt-contender-istanbul-2026-connor-green-anna-hursey-win-mixed-doubles-title.html), winning the decider 11-1. None of the men's seeds reached the semi-finals.

Fang won the 2015 Team World Cup and the 2016 world team title with China and reached the men's singles final at the 2015 World Championships in Suzhou, where he lost to Ma Long. Under the terms of his comeback, Fang does not play in the Olympics, the World Championships or the World Cup.
## Hashimoto recovers from a doubles defeat

Hashimoto had lost the women's doubles final two hours earlier, but the top seed and world No 14 was in control of the singles. She took the first two games 11-9, 11-9, dropped the third 11-7, and then lost only four points in the last two, winning 11-3, 11-1 in 57 minutes.

It is the 28-year-old chopper's first WTT singles title since WTT Contender Almaty in September 2025, after she lost the finals in Lagos and Skopje this year, both to her compatriot Satsuki Odo. She now leads Joo, the world No 17 and second seed, 3-1 in their head-to-head meetings.
Joo, 24, had not dropped a game in the quarter-finals or semi-finals, beating Romania's Bernadette Szőcs and Japan's Kaho Akae. She also reached the mixed doubles semi-finals with Lim Yunoh.
## Doubles titles for Kihara and Hirano and for Artemenko and Grebnev

Japan's Miyuu Kihara and Miu Hirano won the all-Japanese women's doubles final against Hashimoto and Miyu Nagasaki 11-2, 11-8, 11-8 in under half an hour. Hirano had lost to Hashimoto in the singles semi-finals the day before.

In the men's doubles, Russia's Nikita Artemenko and Maksim Grebnev beat Luxembourg's Luka Mladenovic and Mael Van Dessel 11-6, 11-9, 8-11, 11-9. On Saturday, England's Connor Green and Wales's Anna Hursey won the mixed doubles, so China, who had five men in the singles main draw, finished the week without a title in any of the five events.

- Men's singles: Fang Bo (KAZ) bt Kang Dongsoo (KOR) 11-9, 8-11, 11-8, 11-6, 11-9
- Women's singles: Honoka Hashimoto (JPN) bt Joo Cheonhui (KOR) 11-9, 11-9, 7-11, 11-3, 11-1
- Men's doubles: Nikita Artemenko / Maksim Grebnev (RUS) bt Luka Mladenovic / Mael Van Dessel (LUX) 11-6, 11-9, 8-11, 11-9
- Women's doubles: Miyuu Kihara / Miu Hirano (JPN) bt Honoka Hashimoto / Miyu Nagasaki (JPN) 11-2, 11-8, 11-8
- Mixed doubles (Saturday): Connor Green / Anna Hursey (ENG/WAL) bt Evgeny Tikhonov / Maria Panfilova (RUS) 11-7, 12-10, 11-9

Most of the finalists go straight on to WTT Star Contender Muscat, where qualifying starts on Monday and the main draws on Wednesday. Hashimoto and Joo are in the women's main draw, and Fang starts in qualifying against Türkiye's Abdullah Yigenler at about 2.45pm UK time on Monday. Results and the order of play are on Eleven's [Muscat event page](/events/wtt-star-contender-muscat-2026.html#matches).
